Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO qualification (recap + next steps)

Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on SLOs and cost levers.

Summary of customer goals (what I heard):
- Target P95 latency for single-request text generation: ~200ms (streaming endpoints).
- Sustained concurrency target: ~50 concurrent streaming sessions at peak.
- Average request size: ~800 tokens (prompt + response), with some longer sessions up to 2k tokens.
- Hard cost target: keep incremental inference cost to ensure TCO fits their unit economics (Alex asked us to propose options).

Key constraints / ask from FinTechCo:
- Prefer streaming responses for UX (partial tokens as they arrive).
- Low tail latency is a priority for customer-facing flows (trading alerts).
- Compliance: data residency in us-east preferred.

Initial qualification and levers we discussed:
- Continuous batching: aggregate short windows for better GPU utilization; trades off a few ms for throughput efficiency.
- KV/prefix caching: cache repeated prefixes (e.g., user/system prompts) to reduce tokens processed.
- Quantization profiles: int8 or mixed-8 configs for model variants to reduce memory and increase throughput.
- Model variants: suggest a smaller low-latency model for high-concurrency flows and a higher-quality model for occasional long-form generation.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (30-45m) with Vivek to go through streaming shape, concurrency patterns, and test payloads — can you share two representative request samples?
2) We'll provide a cost/perf sketch (ballpark) showing options (dedicated pool vs hosted, quantization tradeoffs, and expected P95).
3) Align on evaluation plan (pilot with 2-4k requests/sec over a day or spike tests) and procurement timeline.

Attachments: I attached a short SLO playbook that outlines our tuning levers.

Availability: I'm free Thu/Fri morning PT for the technical deep-dive. Vivek, Rishi — please chime in if those are good slots.

Alex — thanks, appreciate the specifics. Below are concrete notes we typically run through during the tech deep-dive; I included quick guidance so procurement has something to react to pre-pilot. Vivek/follow-ups will add measured numbers in the riff doc during the call.

SLOs and expected behaviors (high level):
- Streaming P95 target: 200ms is achievable with the right config. We usually see ~150-250ms P95 on modern 80GB/40GB-class GPUs with streaming-optimized kernels for models in the 7B-13B family when using small batching windows and KV caching. For 16GB-class GPUs, quantized int8 + kernel optimizations can be closer to ~220-350ms depending on sequence length.
- Concurrency: 50 sustained concurrent streaming sessions is realistic on a dedicated pool sized appropriately. For spikes (100-120 concurrent short sessions) we'd recommend autoscaling policies with a short warm-up buffer and a fallback (smaller low-latency variant) to maintain SLO.

Cost/performance levers (how we hit your SLOs and the tradeoffs):
1) Continuous batching
   - What it does: collects small requests over a short micro-window (~1-5ms) and runs them as a single GPU batch.
   - Benefit: greatly improves throughput and GPU utilization; cost savings per token.
   - Tradeoff: adds a small added latency cost per request (usually single-digit ms), but for short streaming messages perceived latency is often unchanged due to streaming granularity.

2) KV/prefix caching
   - What it does: cache the key/value cache for repeated prefixes (system prompts, common context).
   - Benefit: avoids recomputing early layers; large token savings for flows with repeated contexts.
   - Tradeoff: additional memory footprint; requires workflow to be cache-friendly (consistent prefixes).

3) Quantization profiles
   - Options: int8, mixed-8, and per-layer tuned profiles.
   - Benefit: reduce model memory and increase throughput; enables fitting larger models on smaller GPUs.
   - Tradeoff: slight quality delta to check (we run evaluation prompts to quantify regression). For many classification/structured generation tasks, int8 is indistinguishable.

4) Model variants & routing
   - Use a high-throughput low-latency variant for interaction-heavy endpoints and a higher-quality variant for batch/long-form results.
   - Smart routing can fallback to a cheaper variant under heavy load to preserve availability.

5) Deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated)
   - Hosted: faster to spin up and test; slightly higher $/token but low ops. Good for PoC.
   - Dedicated: predictable throughput, lower incremental $/token at scale, recommended for production SLOs and heavy concurrency.

Quick ballpark numbers (very rough, we'll refine after sample payloads):
- Hosted: ~$50- $120 per 1M tokens for high-throughput streaming workloads (depends on model family & quantization).
- Dedicated (committed pool): ~$20- $60 per 1M tokens at scale with int8 quantization and continuous batching.

Attachments: I re-attached the SLO playbook and a draft proposal that includes a pilot plan and rough committed-cost scenarios.
